# Judith Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 13

---

**1** When evening came, his servants withdrew in haste. Bagoas closed the tent from outside and dismissed the attendants from before his master's presence. They went away to their beds, for they were all exhausted, because the banquet had lasted a long time.

**2** Judith was left alone in the tent, and Holofernes lay on his bed, drowned in wine.

**3** Judith had told her servant to stand outside the bedchamber and wait for her to come out, as she did every day; for she had said she would go out for her prayer, and she had given Bagoas the same account.

**4** When everyone had gone out and no one, great or small, remained in the bedchamber, Judith stood beside his bed and said in her heart: "O LORD God of all power, look in this hour upon the work of my hands for the exaltation of Jerusalem.

**5** For now is the time to help your inheritance and to accomplish my purpose for the destruction of the enemies who have risen against us."

**6** She went to the bedpost at Holofernes' head and took his sword down from it.

**7** She drew close to the bed, took hold of the hair of his head, and said, "Give me strength, O LORD God of Israel, this day."

**8** She struck his neck twice with all her might and cut off his head.

**9** She rolled his body from the bed and pulled down the canopy from the posts. A moment later she went out and handed the head of Holofernes to her servant,

**10** who put it in her food bag. And the two of them went out together, as they customarily did for prayer. They passed through the camp, circled around the valley, climbed the mountain to Bethulia, and came to its gates.

**11** Judith called out from a distance to the guards at the gates: "Open, open the gate! God is with us — our God — still showing his power in Israel and his might against our enemies, as he has done this very day!"

**12** When the men of her city heard her voice, they rushed down to the city gate and summoned the elders of the city.

**13** Everyone ran together, young and old alike, for her coming was unexpected. They opened the gate and welcomed them in, lit a fire for light, and gathered around them.

**14** She said to them in a loud voice: "Praise God — praise him! Praise God, who has not withdrawn his mercy from the house of Israel, but has shattered our enemies by my hand this night!"

**15** She took the head out of the bag and displayed it before them, saying, "Behold the head of Holofernes, the supreme commander of the Assyrian army — and behold the canopy beneath which he lay drunk. The LORD struck him down by the hand of a woman.

**16** As the LORD lives, who guarded me in the way I walked — it was my face that deceived him to his ruin, and he committed no sin against me to defile and shame me."

**17** All the people were profoundly astonished. They bowed down and worshiped God and said with one voice, "Blessed are you, our God, who this day have brought to shame the enemies of your people."

**18** Uzziah said to her, "Blessed are you, daughter, above all women on the earth; and blessed be the LORD God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the leader of our enemies.

**19** For your hope will never depart from the hearts of men as they remember the power of God forever.

**20** May God make these things a perpetual exaltation to you, and may he visit you with his blessings, because you did not spare your own life when our nation was brought low — but you acted against our ruin, walking in the straight path before our God." And all the people said, "Amen! Amen!"

---

### Council Notes

**On verse 2 — "drowned in wine":** LOGOS' "drowned in wine" (pephyrmenon oinō — lit. "soaked/saturated") is more vivid than EMET's "overcome with wine." SOPHIA adopts "drowned in wine" as both accurate and dramatically precise.

**On verse 8 — THE PIVOTAL SENTENCE:** All three agents render this sentence. The Greek is: kai epataxen ton trachēlon autou dis en tē ischyi autēs kai apheilen tēn kephalēn autou. Literally: "And she struck his neck twice with her strength and took off his head from him."

- EMET: "She struck his neck twice with all her strength, and cut off his head from him."
- LOGOS: "She struck his neck twice with all her might and cut off his head."
- PNEUMA: "She struck his neck with all her might — once, twice — and cut off his head."

**SOPHIA ruling:** "She struck his neck twice with all her might and cut off his head." Direct, precise, complete. The word "twice" (dis) is non-negotiable — it is part of the action and signals physical effort and determination. "All her might" over "all her strength" for euphony. No embellishment. The sentence stands alone in its gravity.

**On verse 9 — "rolled his body from the bed":** EMET's "rolled" is literal and physical (ekulisen). All agents retain this. The physicality is not incidental — the author is writing a realistic account of a real act in a real space.

**On verse 10 — "food bag":** Greek pēra — a traveler's bag. The instrument of disguise: a head in a food bag. The same bag that carried her kosher provisions now carries her trophy.

**On verse 16 — Judith's declaration of purity:** This verse is theologically essential. Judith's first concern upon arriving home is to declare that she was not defiled. This is not incidental — it directly addresses what was at stake throughout chapters 12-13. God preserved her not only to accomplish the mission but to preserve her honor and cleanness. SOPHIA retains the full statement.

**On verse 18 — Uzziah's blessing:** This is a direct echo of multiple biblical blessing formulas. "Blessed are you above all women" — the same formula applied to Jael in Judges 5:24 (Deborah's song). The connection is deliberate and the author intends it.

**On verse 20 — "walking the straight path":** EMET/LOGOS prefer "straight path" (eutheia hodos); PNEUMA paraphrases. SOPHIA retains the path metaphor as it echoes wisdom literature throughout the Hebrew Bible.
